enGB: Psychic spells require thought and emotion components. Concentration checks take a -10 penalty unless Center Self is active. Items and other classes' spellbooks retain their normal restrictions.

enGB:
Your mind is impure, tainted by outside forces. These might be monstrous ancestors whose blood still flows within you, or powerful and unknowable psychic forces that intrude upon your mind. Like a psychic disease, this influence consumes part of your brain, creating a dark counterpart to your normal self. Every time you call forth a psychic spell, you’re drawing on this dangerous force—and potentially giving it a greater hold on you. This malign influence might stem from creatures like rakshasas and aboleths, or perhaps malign entities that dwell in the voids between the stars.
Discipline Powers: Your powers allow the dark influences to take over, and it can be difficult to come back from the brink.
Phrenic Pool Ability: Charisma

enGB: Create a 2-foot-radius electrical globe within medium range for 1 round per caster level. Once per round it affects the first creature occupying or entering its space (allies can be affected); Reflex negates and spell resistance applies. enGB: At 13th level, whenever you cast a spell that deals damage to a creature, you can also make that creature frightened or sickened (your choice) for one round. If you expend two uses of this ability, you can instead have the creature become dazed, nauseated, or panicked for 1 round. The creature can attempt a Will saving throw to negate this effect. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. This is a mind-affecting pain effect.

You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. This is a mind-affecting pain effect.

enGB: Sacrifice any prepared spell or spontaneous spell slot of level 1 to 9 to amplify your next native witch or shaman hex. All three benefits apply together: saving throw DC +slot level, finite effect duration +slot level rounds (if originally at least 1 round), and range +10 feet for levels 1-3, +20 feet for 4-6, or +30 feet for 7-9 (if originally at least 30 feet). Personal/touch range, instantaneous/permanent effects and target cooldowns are unchanged. This is an empowered variant of the tabletop feat. There is no increasing slot-level requirement or daily use cap. Use the spell conversion menu; the sacrificed spell is not cast. Only one hex can be armed. Other spells and abilities do not consume it. Requires a learned supported hex.

enGB: At level 6, rage using the current game's native rage effects, with effective barbarian level equal to cleric/inquisitor level minus 3. Rounds per day are Wisdom modifier plus one per cleric/inquisitor level above 4 (minimum 0). This grants no rage powers, but retains powers you already possess. Greater rage begins at level 14 and tireless rage at level 20. Divine Anger has its own resource and does not refill ordinary barbarian rage.

enGB: Weapon of the Chosen now affects all favored-weapon attacks until the start of your next turn (1 round in real time). Open the single persistent property selector to select one alignment component belonging to your deity for overcoming damage reduction. Selecting another property directly replaces the active property; only one remains active. The five choices are suboptions of one Sacred Weapon-style menu, not separate entries. A wholly neutral deity instead grants both cold iron and silver. The deity's alignment, not your personal alignment, controls availability. Choose before blessing; changing it affects the next blessing. The default is the first available choice. Your weapon retains its original damage type; other weapons and spell damage receive no benefit.

Your weapon retains its original damage type; other weapons and spell damage receive no benefit.

enGB: As a standard action, perform a 30-foot audible masterpiece affecting evil creatures, including evil allies. Each affected creature makes a Will save (DC 10 + half your combined Bard and Skald levels + your Charisma modifier). Evil undead and outsiders are stunned on failure or staggered on success; other evil creatures are blinded on failure or shaken on success. Effects last while the creature hears this performance. This follows original CotW's implemented effects: Wrath has no deafened condition. Normal condition immunities apply. Staggered, blinded and shaken also respect their usual specific-effect immunities. Stun follows original CotW's special rules for this performance. Starting costs 3 performance rounds; each additional round costs 1.

enGB:
By allowing the dark forces to overcome you, you can enter a state of instinctual cruelty as a swift action.
While you’re manifesting your dark half, you increase the DCs of your psychic spells by 1, gain a +2 morale bonus on Will saves, and become immune to fear effects. Whenever you cast a spell that deals damage while manifesting your dark half, you can cause any creature that took damage from the spell to also take 1 point of bleed damage. The amount of bleed damage increases to 2 points at 5th level and to 3 points at 13th level. While manifesting your dark half, you can’t use any Charisma-, Dexterity-, or Intelligence-based skills (except Mobility and Intimidate) or any ability that requires patience or concentration other than casting spells using psychic magic, using phrenic amplifications, or attempting to return to normal. You can attempt to return to your normal self as a free action, but must succeed at an Intelligence check with a DC equal to 10. If you fail, you continue to manifest your dark half and can’t attempt to change back for 1 round.
You can manifest your dark half for a number of rounds per day equal to 3 + 1/2 your psychic level + your Charisma modifier; when these rounds are expended, you return to your normal self without requiring a concentration check.

enGB: A manufactured melee weapon in the target's main hand shines for 1 minute per caster level. Its wielder gains a +1 competence bonus on disarm checks, CMD against disarm, and Bluff checks (including every Feint check), increasing by +1 per 3 caster levels (maximum +5). As a free action, Dazzling Blade: Release ends the spell and flashes at an adjacent enemy: Will failure blinds for 1 round, success dazzles for 1 round. The save uses the original caster's spell DC. The weapon does not become silver. Removing or switching away from the weapon ends the spell.

enGB: Store one self-targeted alchemist extract of 4th level or lower. Release on yourself as a swift action. Duration: 1 day per caster level. Nonqualifying spells cast normally and leave storage armed. Only one storage can be armed per character. Store Next toggles arming off if clicked again. Stored spells retain their original caster, caster level, DC and metamagic across saves. Recasting or dismissing the ward discards its stored spell. Area, multi-target and summon spells cannot be stored. For harmful touch spells, select a legal target as usual; the casting is intercepted before the touch charge is granted. Companion spells with custom external-mod delivery may require separate support.

Your secondary mind can cast Psychic spells and use spell-like abilities of 5th level or lower as swift actions, without increasing their spell slots or costs. Other kinds of purely mental actions are not automated.

enGB: Send an earth tremor in a 20-foot cone, 30-foot line, or 10-foot burst centered on you. Other grounded creatures take 1d4 bludgeoning damage per caster level (maximum 10d4), Reflex half; Medium or smaller creatures that fail fall prone. Rubble patches remain for 1 hour as difficult terrain. Airborne creatures ignore the ground effects. As in Call of the Wild's implementation, the game does not distinguish wood, metal, and earthen floor surfaces for this spell.

enGB: As a free action, project a 30-foot prayer aura for a total number of rounds per day equal to your psychic level. Allies (including you) gain a +1 luck bonus on attack rolls, weapon damage, saving throws and skill checks. Enemies take a -1 penalty to those rolls, or -2 if they oppose you on either the good/evil or lawful/chaotic axis. Opposing both axes still gives only -2. Turning the aura off removes its effects immediately; combat ending, unconsciousness or disability also ends it.

enGB: At psychic level 5, gain a +2 resistance bonus on all saving throws. This bonus increases to +3 at level 10, +4 at level 15 and +5 at level 20. It does not stack with other resistance bonuses.

enGB: When enabled, a hit with a single standard melee attack at full base attack bonus while using Power Attack spends your available swift action to attempt a trip. Full attacks, charges, opportunity attacks, misses and bonus attacks do not trigger it. The normal trip maneuver retains its immunities and checks. Requires Intelligence 13, Strength 13, base attack bonus +6, Combat Expertise, Improved Trip and Power Attack. Ordinary attack commands and native Vital Strike qualify; other separate attack abilities do not.

enGB: Choose one natural attack category. When this animal companion or supported eidolon uses Dexterity for a melee attack with that category and Strength for its damage, it adds one quarter of its own Hit Dice (rounded down) as a bonus to damage. This flat bonus does not change for primary or secondary natural attacks. Requires Weapon Finesse and base attack bonus +3. You may take this feat again for a different natural attack category; the same category does not stack. Dexterity-to-damage attacks do not gain this bonus.

enGB: At 1st level, a feral hunter gains a limited ability to change her shape into hybrid animal forms. This functions as the animal focus class feature, except that the hunter always applies the animal aspect to herself, and there is no limit to this ability’s duration.
zhCN: At 1st level, a feral hunter gains a limited ability to change her shape into hybrid animal forms. This functions as the animal focus class feature, except that the hunter always applies the animal aspect to herself, and there is no limit to this ability’s duration.

enGB: A feral hunter has forged a bond with nature that’s so strong that she doesn’t merely channel the aspects of animals—she actually becomes an animal herself. Though she lacks an animal companion, a feral hunter is in tune with the beast lurking within her flesh and spirit, and lives in a near-wild state of being. A feral hunter often resembles a lycanthrope, but her power comes from her own nature and is not influenced by moonlight or silver.

enGB: At 4th level, a feral hunter gains the ability to change shape. A feral hunter can use wild shape once per day at 4th level and one additional time per day every 2 levels thereafter.

enGB: You can select this feat only at character level 1. Whenever you receive magical healing with dice, heal 2 additional points per healing die. The extra amount is added after Empower and before native healing resistance and the maximum-HP cap; flat healing and natural recovery gain no per-die bonus. Gain +2 on saving throws against death effects. Take 1 additional point of damage from a cold iron weapon hit, once per weapon-damage event, without multiplying this extra point on a critical hit. Cold iron weapon use is otherwise unchanged.
zhCN: You can select this feat only at character level 1. Whenever you receive magical healing with dice, heal 2 additional points per healing die. Gain +2 on saving throws against death effects. Take 1 additional point of damage from a cold iron weapon hit, once per weapon-damage event, without multiplying this extra point on a critical hit. Cold iron weapon use is otherwise unchanged.

enGB: Protect allies in a 15-foot burst within medium range with mobile winds for 1 minute per caster level. Incoming ordinary ranged weapon attacks automatically miss. The protected creatures can fire their own ranged weapons normally. Melee attacks and rays are unaffected. As in Call of the Wild, thrown weapons count as ordinary ranged weapons.

enGB: Create two fiery shuriken plus one per two caster levels beyond 3rd, maximum eight at caster level 15. Each projectile makes its own ranged touch attack for 1d8 fire damage; spell resistance applies and there is no save. Choose to launch all at one target immediately, or launch one and retain the rest for 1 round per caster level. Later, launch one as a swift action, or two to seven as a standard action. Launching retained shuriken does not provoke attacks of opportunity. Recasting replaces any retained shuriken. This follows Call of the Wild's initial one/all selection.

This blocks helpful as well as harmful effects, regardless of spell resistance. Spells can be cast out of or through the globe and affect creatures outside normally. Higher-level spells and supernatural abilities are unaffected. Heighten Spell changes the spell level used for this protection; other metamagic does not. Existing buffs and areas created before the globe are not removed or suppressed. Area dispelling can remove the globe. The globe stays behind if you move; leaving ends its protection, and returning restores it. Uses Call of the Wild's 13-foot area adaptation.

Any creature within 20 feet of you must succeed at a Will save or be confused for 1d4 rounds. A creature that succeeds at its saving throw is immune to your hallucinogenic aura for 24 hours. enGB: Invite facets of your patron into yourself. Select one facet using the free preference toggles, then use Invoke Patron as a swift action to gain the selected benefit for 1 minute. Each activation consumes 1 minute from a daily pool equal to your witch level, including reactivation before the previous minute ends. Preference changes apply to your next invocation. At witch level 10 you may select two different facets. Replaces the hexes at levels 1, 8, 10 and 16; the familiar, patron, spellbook and other hexes are retained.

enGB: A melee touch attack makes the target dance in place, unable to take other actions, for 1d4 + 1 rounds. It takes a -4 penalty to AC and a -10 penalty on Reflex saves, loses the AC bonuses of its held shield, and provokes attacks of opportunity each round. A successful Will save reduces the duration to 1 round. Spell resistance and mind-affecting compulsion immunities apply. A missed touch retains the charge.

enGB: Requires monk level 20. Spend 3 ki points to apply Akashic Form to yourself, using its original action and duration. Caster level equals monk level. Requires PrestigePlus's Akashic Form; its out-of-combat restriction remains. Sensei Mystic Wisdom permits a single ally for 1 additional ki, or allies within 30 feet for 2 additional ki after the mass improvement. For 24 hours preserve the recipient with the provider spell's life-saving effect. The preparation requires a full-round action outside combat.

enGB: Requires Wisdom 13, Improved Unarmed Strike and base attack bonus +3. While using this combat style, take -2 AC against melee attacks (including melee touch attacks). After an enemy makes a melee weapon attack against you, your unarmed strikes against that enemy use your positive Wisdom modifier for damage if it exceeds the current Strength or Dexterity modifier. The opening lasts until the beginning of that enemy's next turn (six seconds in real time). Other damage statistics, weapons and targets are unchanged.

enGB: Create mage's sword for 1 round per caster level. It attacks your designated enemy and can be redirected with a move action. Casting allows one attack; redirecting after an attack changes the next attack without granting an extra attack that round. Later rounds allow normal iterative attacks (Mage's Sword and Twilight Knife attack once). Attacks use your base attack bonus and highest mental ability modifier; Mage's Sword instead uses caster level plus that modifier +3. Force damage ignores physical damage reduction and incorporeal resistance. A failed spell resistance check ends this casting. You may dismiss it as a free action. Only one of each kind can be maintained by a caster. Mage's Sword deals 4d6+3 force damage. The floating weapon is a longsword. Retargeting moves it to the target's vicinity. The spell controller schedules attacks at six-second round boundaries; enemy movement does not consume additional caster actions.

enGB: At 11th level, you can select major amplifications in place of phrenic amplifications. This feature grants eligibility, not an additional selection.

enGB: At 3rd level, a psychic marauder’s madness begins to leak out. As a standard action, the psychic marauder can spend 1 point from her phrenic pool to manifest an aura of insanity, letting bits of her psyche penetrate the minds of those around her. The aura is centered on the psychic marauder and has a radius of 10 feet, increasing by 5 feet for every 3 class levels beyond 3rd. Any hostile creature starting its turn within the aura must succeed at a Will save (DC = 10 + half the psychic marauder’s level + the psychic marauder’s Intelligence modifier) or be confused for 1 round. The aura of insanity lasts for a number of rounds equal to the psychic marauder’s Charisma modifier. This is a mind-affecting effect.

enGB: When the psychic gains this amplification, she chooses two metamagic feats; she need not have these feats to select them. When she casts a spell, she can spend points from her phrenic pool to apply one of the chosen feats to the linked spell without increasing the spell’s level or casting time. She must spend a number of points equal to double the number of levels by which the feat normally increases a spell’s level (minimum 2 points). If the metamagic feat alters the spell’s casting time in a different way than the standard rules for a spontaneous caster using a metamagic feat (as in the case of Quicken Spell), it changes the casting time accordingly. The psychic can still apply metamagic feats she knows to the spell while using this amplification, increasing the casting time and spell level as normal. This amplification can be applied only to a spell that the chosen metamagic feat could normally affect, and only if the spellcaster can cast spells of a high enough level that she would be able to apply the metamagic feat in question to the linked spell. For example, an 11th-level psychic could spend 8 points to quicken a 1st-level spell, but couldn’t quicken a 2nd-level spell because she’s unable to cast 6th-level spells. This ability doesn’t require her to have any free spell slots in the relevant level, however, so the psychic in the example could quicken a 1st-level spell even if she had cast all her 5th-level spells for the day. A psychic can select this amplification multiple times, adding two additional options to the list of metamagic feats she can apply using this amplification each time.

enGB:
As a swift action, you can cause an enemy to take 1d6 points of damage if you dealt damage to that enemy with a spell since the start of your previous turn. enGB: A mutation mind’s psychic powers warp her body, allowing her to physically mutate herself as a swift action, which grants her a +4 alchemical bonus to Strength and a –2 penalty to Intelligence. At 12th level, the bonus to Strength increases to +6, and at 16th level to +8. A mutation mind can assume her physically mutated form for a number of minutes per day equal to her psychic level. The minutes don’t have to be used consecutively, but must be used in 1-minute increments. After the mutation ends, the mutation mind is fatigued and can’t activate a physical mutation again for 1 round.

enGB: When using druid wild shape to take an animal form or an eligible shifter major form, you may spend one additional wild shape use to gain the celestial or fiendish template for that form. Good characters may choose only celestial; evil characters only fiendish; neutral characters may choose either. Select the persistent template before transforming. Animal forms gain the native template's spell resistance, energy resistances, damage reduction and daily smite, scaled to your own Hit Dice. Natural-weapon critical confirmation rolls gain +2 against the opposite alignment. Elemental and plant forms do not spend the extra use or gain the template. Master Shapeshifter and native unlimited-major-form features waive all wild-shape cost, including the extra use. Rageshaper Devastating Form and Fiendflesh Shifter Fiendish Aspect are excluded. Requires wild shape and Lore (Religion) 5 ranks.

Animal forms gain the native template's spell resistance, energy resistances, damage reduction and daily smite, scaled to your own Hit Dice. Natural-weapon critical confirmation rolls gain +2 against the opposite alignment. Elemental and plant forms do not spend the extra use or gain the template. Master Shapeshifter and native unlimited-major-form features waive all wild-shape cost, including the extra use. Rageshaper Devastating Form and Fiendflesh Shifter Fiendish Aspect are excluded. Requires wild shape and Lore (Religion) 5 ranks.

enGB:
Each sorcerer has a source of magic somewhere in her heritage that grants her spells, bonus feats, an additional class skill, and other special abilities. This source can represent a blood relation or an extreme event involving a creature somewhere in the family's past. For example, a sorcerer might have a dragon as a distant relative or her grandfather might have signed a terrible contract with a devil. Regardless of the source, this influence manifests in a number of ways as the sorcerer gains levels. A sorcerer must pick one bloodline upon taking her first level of sorcerer. Once made, this choice cannot be changed.
Filled with magical power that screams for release, sorcery is not so much a calling as a blessing — or a curse. For some sorcerers, this arcane birthright manifests in subtle and carefully controlled ways, assisting in their manipulation of others or the pursuit of lofty goals. For others, it is wild and unpredictable, the primal and explosive lashing out of a power greater than themselves.
At 3rd level, and every two levels thereafter, a sorcerer learns an additional spell, derived from her bloodline. These spells are in addition to the number of spells given at new levels. These spells cannot be exchanged for different spells at higher levels.
At 7th level, and every six levels thereafter, a sorcerer receives one bonus feat, chosen from a list specific to each bloodline. The sorcerer must meet the prerequisites for these bonus feats.

enGB:
Once per day, you can create a cognatogen, a mutagen-like mixture that heightens one mental ability score at the expense of a physical ability score. When you imbibe a cognatogen, you gain a +2 natural armor bonus and a +4 alchemical bonus to the selected ability score for 1 minute per psychic level. In addition, while the cognatogen is in effect, you take a –2 penalty to one of your physical ability scores. If the cognatogen enhances your Intelligence, it applies a penalty to your Strength. If it enhances your Wisdom, it applies a penalty to your Dexterity.
If it enhances your Charisma, it applies a penalty to your Constitution. Otherwise, this ability works just like the alchemist’s mutagen ability. When the effect of the cognatogen ends, you take 2 points of ability damage to the ability score penalized by the cognatogen. If you have both alchemist and psychic levels, these levels stack to determine the duration of your cognatogen and the DC of the save a non-alchemist must attempt if he drinks your cognatogen. If you gain discoveries, you can take the grand cognatogen and greater cognatogen discoveries to improve your cognatogen. The infuse mutagen discovery and the persistent mutagen class ability apply to cognatogens. However, even if you have alchemist levels, the duration of your cognatogen remains 1 minute per level (instead of 10 minutes per level).

enGB: Crush a creature's mind. A successful Will save sickens the target for 1 round. A failed Will save requires a Fortitude save: success deals 3d6 direct damage plus your caster level and sickens the target for 1 round; failure reduces it to -1 HP. Damage from this spell cannot reduce HP below -1. The Fortitude save gains a +4 circumstance bonus if the target has more than half its maximum HP. Temporary HP does not affect these thresholds. Mind-affecting immunity and spell resistance apply. As in CotW, constructs and vermin cannot be targeted.

enGB: Restore all Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma damage and drain. Remove ongoing fear and confusion effects. Also remove harmful mind-affecting or enchantment effects: dispellable spell effects of any spell level, or other effects of spell level 6 or lower. Beneficial mental effects, physical ability damage, and effects without a removable ongoing buff are unaffected. Requires the same diamond dust component as Stoneskin.

enGB: As a standard action, spend 2 phrenic points and sacrifice a Psychic spell slot of 2nd level or higher. Gain an enhancement bonus to Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution equal to the slot's level for 1 minute per psychic level. Choose the conversion under a known Psychic spell of that level; the original spell is not cast. Enhancement bonuses to the same attribute do not stack.

enGB: As a swift action, arm your next bloodrager spell for 1 round. Choose 1 to 4 damage dice; the actual number is capped by that spell's slot level. Gain that many points of saving throw DC and lose that many d6 hit points when the spell is attempted. This loss bypasses temporary hit points, resistances and damage reduction and cannot be reduced by damage modifiers. Items, cantrips and spells from other classes do not trigger it. Only one choice can be armed. Requires bloodrager level 4. A native failed spell that still spends its slot also pays this cost; canceled commands and forced failures do not.

enGB: A Rogue archetype focused on martial training and daring acrobatics. This is a Rogue archetype, separate from any standalone Swashbuckler class.

enGB: Requires Constitution 13. enGB: Create a movable 20-foot-radius sandstorm within medium range for 1 round per caster level. On entry and each round, creatures take 3d6 piercing damage (at most once per creature per round). Medium or smaller creatures must pass a DC10 Strength check to move; Small or smaller creatures also need DC15 Strength or fall prone and take2d6 bludgeoning damage. Air-subtype creatures ignore movement/visibility effects, but still take sand damage. The storm grants total fog concealment, blocks sight-based effects, slows movement, and prevents ordinary ranged weapon attacks into or out of it; rays are not automatically blocked. Move it with a move action, retaining remaining duration and original casting parameters. Repositioning does not sweep the path. No save or spell resistance applies; allies can be affected.

enGB: Create spiritual ally for 1 round per caster level. It attacks your designated enemy and can be redirected with a move action. Casting allows one attack; redirecting after an attack changes the next attack without granting an extra attack that round. Later rounds allow normal iterative attacks (Mage's Sword and Twilight Knife attack once). Attacks use your base attack bonus and highest mental ability modifier; Mage's Sword instead uses caster level plus that modifier +3. Force damage ignores physical damage reduction and incorporeal resistance. A failed spell resistance check ends this casting. You may dismiss it as a free action. Only one of each kind can be maintained by a caster. Each hit deals 1d8 force damage +1 per 3 caster levels (maximum +5). Spiritual Ally threatens adjacent enemies and can flank and make attacks of opportunity, using the normal per-round opportunity limit. Choose Chaos (battleaxe), Evil (light flail), Good (warhammer), Law (longsword), or your deity's favored weapon. Critical threat and multiplier follow that weapon. These choices are not restricted by your alignment. If your deity has multiple favored weapons, its first supported native category is used. Retargeting moves it to the target's vicinity. The spell controller schedules attacks at six-second round boundaries; enemy movement does not consume additional caster actions.

Companion spells with custom external-mod delivery may require separate support.

enGB: Extract the air from living creatures that must breathe. Fortitude success causes only 1 round of staggered. On failure, the subject is staggered and begins to suffocate. Starting on its next round, a failed Fortitude save advances one step: reduce hit points to 0, then to -1, then death. Successful later saves delay progression without ending the spell. The single-target spell lasts 3 rounds; the mass spell affects enemies in a 30-foot burst for 1 round per caster level. Undead, constructs and elementals are excluded. This is a death effect.

enGB: Enemies must already be shaken: this howl does not inflict shaken by itself. While raging or accepting inspired rage, use a standard action to frighten shaken enemies within 30 feet for 1d4+1 rounds (Will negates; DC 10 + half your barbarian/skald/primalist level + your Strength modifier). A creature that attempts this save is immune to your howl for 24 hours, whether it succeeds or fails. Targets that are not shaken, cannot hear the howl because of silence, or still have this caster's 24-hour immunity do not attempt a save. Requires barbarian, skald or primalist level 8. Inspired rage grants this ability through the native sharing mechanism, like Renewed Vigor; the character using the howl is its caster.

enGB: Time appears to stop for all other creatures while you act for 1d4+1 rounds. Other creatures in the area cannot act, move or attack, and cannot be targeted or damaged until the effect ends. You can move and cast spells on yourself, or place area spells whose remaining duration continues after time resumes. This personal, standard-action transmutation is a 9th-level wizard, sorcerer, arcanist and psychic spell. It has no saving throw or spell resistance. It does not grant Time Stutter or use that discovery's daily resource. While this spell is active, use Time Stop: End as a free action to resume time early.

enGB: You briefly step out of time, using the game's Time Stop effect for 1 round. All other creatures in the area become unable to act, move or attack and cannot be targeted or damaged while the effect lasts. This spell-like ability uses a standard action and can be used once per day, plus one additional time at wizard levels 15 and 20. Requires wizard level 10 or arcanist level 20. Arcanist levels count at half their value; class levels are not added together. Time Stutter can only be selected within Arcane Discovery, and does not grant the Time Stop spell.

enGB: A toppling spell uses a spell slot one level higher. When a spell with the force descriptor deals damage to a creature, attempt to trip that creature using caster level instead of base attack bonus and the spell's casting ability instead of Strength. A ray must hit, and actual damage must be dealt. Use the game's normal trip immunity and CMD rules. One check per damaged creature per casting; multiple missiles do not repeat the same check. No extra action or attack of opportunity is required.

No extra action or attack of opportunity is required.

enGB: At 1st level, the connection the totem-bonded has with her animal companion allows them to draw upon one another’s strength. The totem-bonded can activate this ability as a swift action, and she can use it for a number of minutes per day equal to her level. This duration does not need to be consecutive, but it must be spent in 1-minute increments. While active, select one aspect: +1 natural armor, +10 feet speed, two claws (1d4), bite (1d6), gore (1d6), or slam (1d6). Only natural attacks possessed by the chosen companion are available. At 8th level, select two aspects; natural armor and speed improve to +2 and +20 feet, and increased size and powerful charge become available. At 15th level, natural attack damage increases two die steps. At 20th level, select three aspects. The companion also receives +1 on saves and +2 on Athletics, Mobility, Stealth and Perception, increasing to +2/+4 at 8th level and +3/+6 at 15th level. Select aspects with their persistent switches, then activate Shared Strength for one minute. Selecting an aspect costs no use.

The wound follows normal bleed cleanup outside combat.

enGB: Create twilight knife for 1 round per caster level. It attacks your designated enemy and can be redirected with a move action. Casting allows one attack; redirecting after an attack changes the next attack without granting an extra attack that round. Later rounds allow normal iterative attacks (Mage's Sword and Twilight Knife attack once). Attacks use your base attack bonus and highest mental ability modifier; Mage's Sword instead uses caster level plus that modifier +3. Force damage ignores physical damage reduction and incorporeal resistance. A failed spell resistance check ends this casting. You may dismiss it as a free action. Only one of each kind can be maintained by a caster. Twilight Knife deals 1d4 force damage plus 1d6 sneak attack per 4 caster levels when the normal sneak attack conditions apply. It automatically follows the target of your weapon attacks, at most once per round. The floating weapon is a dagger. Retargeting moves it to the target's vicinity. The spell controller schedules attacks at six-second round boundaries; enemy movement does not consume additional caster actions.

enGB: When the psychic undercasts a spell, she can spend points from her phrenic pool to increase the spell’s effective level, essentially using up a lower-level spell slot to cast a higher-level version of the spell. This costs 2 points per spell level increased. She can’t use this ability to cast a version higher than the version she knows. For instance, a psychic who knows mind thrust III but not mind thrust IV could cast mind thrust II and spend 2 points to treat it as mind thrust III, but couldn’t spend 4 points to treat it as mind thrust IV. This amplification can be linked only to spells that can be undercast. Enable the desired tier and cast the lower version normally. It executes the matching higher version available within your known spell family, spends the lower slot, and costs two phrenic points per tier. No eligible higher version or insufficient points leaves the ordinary spell unamplified and spends no phrenic points.

enGB: Requires Combat Reflexes and Improved Unarmed Strike. When an enemy falls prone adjacent to you, it provokes one unarmed attack of opportunity. This uses the game's successful knockdown event, an unarmed threat hand, adjacency (5 feet), normal target legality and the native opportunity-attack allowance. Remaining prone or standing up does not trigger this feat again. An ordinary stand-up opportunity attack retains its own native rules. Greater Trip and this feat share the native opportunity-attack limits.

enGB: Choose unarmed strikes, claws, bites, gore or other natural weapons. For 1 minute per caster level, hits with that category deal an extra 1d6 piercing damage, not multiplied on critical hits. Once per target per round, a hit also allows a Reflex save; failure entangles that target for 1 round. This uses Call of the Wild's one-round entangle implementation. The same caster cannot force another vine save on that target during that round, even after a successful save. Different chosen categories can coexist; repeated castings for the same category do not stack.

The total increases to +6 at bloodrager level 11 and +8 at 20. Then activate Controlled Bloodrage. It grants none of the ordinary bloodrage attack, damage, temporary hit point, Will or AC adjustments. It counts as bloodrage for bloodline powers and prerequisites. Native rage rounds, fatigue restrictions and Limitless Rage are retained. Charisma-, Dexterity- and Intelligence-based skills remain usable.

enGB: Mental blocks have obscured an amnesiac's former psychic power. Recollect forgotten spells from the recesses of memory.
zhCN: Mental blocks have obscured an amnesiac's former psychic power. Recollect forgotten spells from the recesses of memory.

enGB:
For 1 round, gain a +8 enhancement bonus to Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (choose when casting). You are dazed for 1 round afterward.

As a swift action, attempt to recall an unknown spell from the current Psychic list in a circle with an available amnesia slot. Outside combat, Recollection has a one-hour cooldown. In combat it ignores that cooldown and adds d10 to the d100 roll; a spell recalled in combat must be cast before the start of your next turn or it is forgotten. A successful cast, including a metamagic version, retains it until rest. 1-10: unable to cast spells for one round. 11-35: no spell recalled. 36-95: recall the spell. 96+: also refund the amnesia slot. Recollection uses no ordinary spell slot or phrenic points; casting uses ordinary slots. Recalled knowledge is cleared when beginning a level-up, preserving paid knowledge.

enGB:

The missile strikes unerringly, even if the target is in melee combat, so long as it has less than total cover or total {g|Encyclopedia:Concealment}concealment{/g}. Specific parts of a creature can't be singled out. Objects are not {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damaged{/g} by the {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell{/g}.
For every two {g|Encyclopedia:Caster_Level}caster levels{/g} beyond 1st, you gain an additional missile — two at 3rd level, three at 5th, four at 7th, and the maximum of five missiles at 9th level or higher.

As a swift action, attempt to recall an unknown spell from the current Psychic list in a circle with an available amnesia slot. Outside combat, Recollection has a one-hour cooldown. In combat it ignores that cooldown and adds d10 to the d100 roll; a spell recalled in combat must be cast before the start of your next turn or it is forgotten. A successful cast, including a metamagic version, retains it until rest. 1-10: unable to cast spells for one round. 11-35: no spell recalled. 36-95: recall the spell. 96+: also refund the amnesia slot. Recollection uses no ordinary spell slot or phrenic points; casting uses ordinary slots. Recalled knowledge is cleared when beginning a level-up, preserving paid knowledge.

enGB:
The subject's outline appears blurred, shifting, and wavering. This distortion grants the subject {g|Encyclopedia:Concealment}concealment{/g} (20% miss chance).
A {g|SpellsSeeInvisibility}see invisibility{/g} spell does not counteract the blur effect, but a {g|SpellsTrueSeeing}true seeing{/g} spell does.
Opponents that cannot see the subject ignore the spell's effect (though fighting an unseen opponent carries penalties of its own).

enGB:
This abjuration grants a creature limited protection from {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} of whichever one of five energy types you select: acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic. The subject gains {g|Encyclopedia:Energy_Resistance}resist{/g} energy 10 against the energy type chosen, meaning that each time the creature is subjected to such damage (whether from a natural or magical source), that damage is reduced by 10 points before being applied to the creature's {g|Encyclopedia:HP}hit points{/g}. Resist energy absorbs only damage. The subject could still suffer unfortunate side effects. Resist energy doesn't stack with {g|SpellsProtectionFromEnergy}protection from energy{/g}. If a character is warded by protection from energy and resist energy, the protection {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell{/g} absorbs damage until its power is exhausted. The value of the energy resistance granted increases to 20 points at 7th level and to a maximum of 30 points at 11th level.

enGB:
For 1 minute per caster level, each damage event that deals at least 5 points of piercing or slashing damage to you gives your worn armor a +1 enhancement bonus, to a maximum of +5. This does not stack with an existing armor enhancement bonus; use the higher value. Count damage after reduction, and increase the bonus only once per damage event. Requires worn armor. Removing your armor suspends the armor bonus; another suit you equip receives your accumulated enhancement. Recasting resets the accumulated bonus.

enGB:
This {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell{/g} creates a number of illusory doubles of you that inhabit your space. These doubles make it difficult for enemies to precisely locate and {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack{/g} you.
When mirror image is cast, {g|Encyclopedia:Dice}1d4{/g} images plus one image per three {g|Encyclopedia:Caster_Level}caster levels{/g} (maximum eight images total) are created. These images remain in your space and move with you, mimicking your movements, sounds, and {g|Encyclopedia:CA_Types}actions{/g} exactly. Whenever you are attacked or are the target of a spell that requires an attack roll, there is a possibility that the attack targets one of your images instead. If the attack is a hit, roll randomly to see whether the selected target is real or a figment. If it is a figment, the figment is destroyed. If the attack misses by 5 or less, one of your figments is destroyed by the near miss. Area spells affect you normally and do not destroy any of your figments. Spells and effects that do not require an attack roll affect you normally and do not destroy any of your figments. Spells that require a {g|Encyclopedia:TouchAttack}touch attack{/g} are harmlessly discharged if used to destroy a figment.
An attacker must be able to see the figments to be fooled. If you are {g|ConditionInvisible}invisible{/g} or the attacker is {g|ConditionBlind}blind{/g}, the spell has no effect (although the normal miss chances still apply).

As a swift action, attempt to recall an unknown spell from the current Psychic list in a circle with an available amnesia slot. Outside combat, Recollection has a one-hour cooldown. In combat it ignores that cooldown and adds d10 to the d100 roll; a spell recalled in combat must be cast before the start of your next turn or it is forgotten. A successful cast, including a metamagic version, retains it until rest. 1-10: unable to cast spells for one round. 11-35: no spell recalled. 36-95: recall the spell. 96+: also refund the amnesia slot. Recollection uses no ordinary spell slot or phrenic points; casting uses ordinary slots. Recalled knowledge is cleared when beginning a level-up, preserving paid knowledge.

enGB:
Enemies in a 30-foot burst within close range suffer wracking pain for 1 round per caster level. They take a -2 penalty to AC, attack rolls, melee weapon damage and Reflex saves. Casting a spell requires a concentration check (DC 15 + spell level). Fortitude negates; spell resistance applies. The pain cannot be relieved by spending an action to scream.

enGB:
The affected creature gains greater vitality and stamina. The {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell{/g} grants the subject a +4 enhancement {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Constitution}Constitution{/g}, which adds the usual benefits to {g|Encyclopedia:HP}hit points{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Fortitude saves{/g}, Constitution {g|Encyclopedia:Check}checks{/g}, and so forth. Hit points gained by a temporary increase in Constitution score are not {g|Encyclopedia:Temporary_HP}temporary hit points{/g}. They go away when the subject's Constitution drops back to normal. They are not lost first as temporary hit points are.

enGB:
The target becomes smarter. The {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell{/g} grants a +4 enhancement {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Intelligence}Intelligence{/g}, adding the usual benefits to Intelligence-based {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Check}checks{/g} and other uses of the Intelligence modifier. Wizards (and other spellcasters who rely on Intelligence) affected by this spell do not gain any additional bonus spells for the increased Intelligence, but the {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}save{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:DC}DCs{/g} for spells they cast while under this spell's effect do increase. This spell doesn't grant extra skill ranks.

You hurl a fist-sized ball of force resembling a sphere of spikes to ram a designated creature. You must succeed on a ranged {g|Encyclopedia:TouchAttack}touch attack{/g} to strike your target. On a successful hit, you deal {g|Encyclopedia:Dice}1d6{/g} points of {g|Encyclopedia:Energy_Damage}force damage{/g} per two caster levels (maximum 5d6). For every 5 caster levels you possess beyond 5th, you gain an additional ball of force.
A creature struck by any of these is subject to a bull rush attempt. The force has a {g|Encyclopedia:Strength}Strength{/g} modifier equal to your {g|Encyclopedia:Intelligence}Intelligence{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Wisdom}Wisdom{/g}, or {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g} modifier (whichever is highest). The {g|Encyclopedia:CMB}CMB{/g} for the force's bull rush uses your {g|Encyclopedia:Caster_Level}caster level{/g} as its {g|Encyclopedia:BAB}base attack bonus{/g}, adding the force's Strength modifier and a +10 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} for each additional blast that hits. If the bull rush succeeds, the force pushes the creature away from you in a straight line, and the creature must make a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Reflex save{/g} or fall {g|ConditionProne}prone{/g}.

enGB:
Create twilight knife for 1 round per caster level. It attacks your designated enemy and can be redirected with a move action. Casting allows one attack; redirecting after an attack changes the next attack without granting an extra attack that round. Later rounds allow normal iterative attacks (Mage's Sword and Twilight Knife attack once). Attacks use your base attack bonus and highest mental ability modifier; Mage's Sword instead uses caster level plus that modifier +3. Force damage ignores physical damage reduction and incorporeal resistance. A failed spell resistance check ends this casting. You may dismiss it as a free action. Only one of each kind can be maintained by a caster. Twilight Knife deals 1d4 force damage plus 1d6 sneak attack per 4 caster levels when the normal sneak attack conditions apply. It automatically follows the target of your weapon attacks, at most once per round. The floating weapon is a dagger. Retargeting moves it to the target's vicinity. The spell controller schedules attacks at six-second round boundaries; enemy movement does not consume additional caster actions.

A successful cast, including a metamagic version, retains it until rest. 1-10: unable to cast spells for one round. 11-35: no spell recalled. 36-95: recall the spell. 96+: also refund the amnesia slot. Recollection uses no ordinary spell slot or phrenic points; casting uses ordinary slots. Recalled knowledge is cleared when beginning a level-up, preserving paid knowledge.

enGB:
This {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell{/g} causes instant growth of all allied humanoid creatures in 15 feet, doubling their height and multiplying their weight by 8. This increase changes the creature's {g|Encyclopedia:Size}size{/g} category to the next larger one. A humanoid creature whose size increases to Large has a space of 10 feet and a natural {g|Encyclopedia:Reach}reach{/g} of 10 feet. This spell does not change the targets' {g|Encyclopedia:Speed}speed{/g}.
Enlarge person dispels {g|SpellsReducePerson}reduce person{/g}.

enGB:
You create a phantasmal image of the most fearsome creature imaginable to the subject simply by forming the fears of the subject's subconscious mind into something that its conscious mind can visualize: this most horrible beast. Only the {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell's{/g} subject can see the phantasmal killer. You see only a vague shape. The target first gets a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Will save{/g} to recognize the image as unreal. If that save fails, the phantasm touches the subject, and the subject must succeed at a Fortitude save or die from fear. Even if the Fortitude save is successful, the subject takes {g|Encyclopedia:Dice}3d6{/g} points of {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g}.

enGB:
Create a stationary 13-foot-radius globe centered on your current position for 1 round per caster level. Creatures inside are protected from newly applied spells and spell-like abilities of level 3 or lower, including cantrips and spells from items. This blocks helpful as well as harmful effects, regardless of spell resistance. Spells can be cast out of or through the globe and affect creatures outside normally. Higher-level spells and supernatural abilities are unaffected. Heighten Spell changes the spell level used for this protection; other metamagic does not. Existing buffs and areas created before the globe are not removed or suppressed. Area dispelling can remove the globe. The globe stays behind if you move; leaving ends its protection, and returning restores it. Uses Call of the Wild's 13-foot area adaptation.

enGB:
Protection from energy grants all allies within a 25-foot radius temporary immunity to the type of energy you specify when you cast it (acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic). Once the {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell{/g} absorbs 12 points of {g|Encyclopedia:Energy_Damage}energy damage{/g} per {g|Encyclopedia:Caster_Level}caster level{/g} (maximum 120 points) for a subject, the spell's effects end for that subject.

As a swift action, attempt to recall an unknown spell from the current Psychic list in a circle with an available amnesia slot. Outside combat, Recollection has a one-hour cooldown. In combat it ignores that cooldown and adds d10 to the d100 roll; a spell recalled in combat must be cast before the start of your next turn or it is forgotten. A successful cast, including a metamagic version, retains it until rest. 1-10: unable to cast spells for one round. 11-35: no spell recalled. 36-95: recall the spell. 96+: also refund the amnesia slot. Recollection uses no ordinary spell slot or phrenic points; casting uses ordinary slots. Recalled knowledge is cleared when beginning a level-up, preserving paid knowledge.

enGB:
This {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell{/g} frees victims from enchantments, transmutations, and curses. Break enchantment can reverse even an instantaneous effect. For each such effect, you make a {g|Encyclopedia:Caster_Level}caster level{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Check}check{/g} ({g|Encyclopedia:Dice}1d20{/g} + caster level, maximum +15) against a {g|Encyclopedia:DC}DC{/g} of 11 + caster level of the effect. Success means that the creature is free of the spell, curse, or effect. Break enchantment only works on spells of 5th level or lower.

enGB:
Ill fortune surrounds the target for 1 round per caster level. Whenever it deals damage, it must attempt a Will save (DC 10 + half your caster level + your highest Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier). Failure halves that damage. There is no initial saving throw; spell resistance applies. This follows Call of the Wild: the save is made for each damage event, including each target of an area spell.

A melee touch attack overloads the target's synapses, dealing 1d6 electricity damage per caster level (maximum 15d6) and staggering it for 1 minute. Fortitude negates only the staggered effect, not the damage. A missed touch retains the charge.

As a swift action, attempt to recall an unknown spell from the current Psychic list in a circle with an available amnesia slot. Outside combat, Recollection has a one-hour cooldown. In combat it ignores that cooldown and adds d10 to the d100 roll; a spell recalled in combat must be cast before the start of your next turn or it is forgotten. A successful cast, including a metamagic version, retains it until rest. 1-10: unable to cast spells for one round. 11-35: no spell recalled. 36-95: recall the spell. 96+: also refund the amnesia slot. Recollection uses no ordinary spell slot or phrenic points; casting uses ordinary slots. Recalled knowledge is cleared when beginning a level-up, preserving paid knowledge.

enGB:
Crush a creature's mind. A successful Will save sickens the target for 1 round. A failed Will save requires a Fortitude save: success deals 3d6 direct damage plus your caster level and sickens the target for 1 round; failure reduces it to -1 HP. Damage from this spell cannot reduce HP below -1. The Fortitude save gains a +4 circumstance bonus if the target has more than half its maximum HP. Temporary HP does not affect these thresholds. Mind-affecting immunity and spell resistance apply. As in CotW, constructs and vermin cannot be targeted.

enGB:
Create a stationary 13-foot-radius globe centered on your current position for 1 round per caster level. Creatures inside are protected from newly applied spells and spell-like abilities of level 4 or lower, including cantrips and spells from items. This blocks helpful as well as harmful effects, regardless of spell resistance. Spells can be cast out of or through the globe and affect creatures outside normally. Higher-level spells and supernatural abilities are unaffected. Heighten Spell changes the spell level used for this protection; other metamagic does not. Existing buffs and areas created before the globe are not removed or suppressed. Area dispelling can remove the globe. The globe stays behind if you move; leaving ends its protection, and returning restores it. Uses Call of the Wild's 13-foot area adaptation.

A failed Will save requires a Fortitude save: success deals 5d6 direct damage plus your caster level and sickens the target for 1 round; failure reduces it to -1 HP. Damage from this spell cannot reduce HP below -1. The Fortitude save gains a +4 circumstance bonus at full HP, or +2 above half HP. Temporary HP does not affect these thresholds. Mind-affecting immunity and spell resistance apply. As in CotW, constructs and vermin cannot be targeted. This spell can be undercast.

enGB:
Crush a creature's mind. A successful Will save deals 1 direct damage per caster level and sickens the target for 1 round. A failed Will save requires a Fortitude save: success deals 7d6 direct damage plus your caster level and sickens the target for 1 round; failure reduces it to -1 HP. Damage from this spell cannot reduce HP below -1. The Fortitude save gains a +2 circumstance bonus at full HP. Temporary HP does not affect these thresholds. Mind-affecting immunity and spell resistance apply. As in CotW, constructs and vermin cannot be targeted. This spell can be undercast.

enGB:
Create mage's sword for 1 round per caster level. It attacks your designated enemy and can be redirected with a move action. Casting allows one attack; redirecting after an attack changes the next attack without granting an extra attack that round. Later rounds allow normal iterative attacks (Mage's Sword and Twilight Knife attack once). Attacks use your base attack bonus and highest mental ability modifier; Mage's Sword instead uses caster level plus that modifier +3. Force damage ignores physical damage reduction and incorporeal resistance. A failed spell resistance check ends this casting. You may dismiss it as a free action. Only one of each kind can be maintained by a caster. Mage's Sword deals 4d6+3 force damage. The floating weapon is a longsword. Retargeting moves it to the target's vicinity. The spell controller schedules attacks at six-second round boundaries; enemy movement does not consume additional caster actions.

You speak a terrible word of power, setting up potentially lethal vibrations in the chosen target. The target must make a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Fortitude saving throw{/g} once each {g|Encyclopedia:Combat_Round}round{/g}, and the effects grow stronger for each saving throw the creature fails.
On the first round, the target takes {g|Encyclopedia:Dice}5d6{/g} points of {g|Encyclopedia:Energy_Damage}sonic damage{/g} and is {g|ConditionStaggered}staggered{/g} for 1 round. A successful save halves the damage and negates the staggered effect.
On the second round, the target takes 5d6 points of damage and is {g|ConditionStunned}stunned{/g} for 1 round. A successful save halves the damage and negates the stunning effect.

The resonating word has no power after the third round, even if the {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell's{/g} duration is increased.

enGB:
Crush a creature's mind. A successful Will save deals 9d6 direct damage plus your caster level and sickens the target for 1 round. A failed Will save requires a Fortitude save: success deals 9d6 direct damage plus your caster level and sickens the target for 1 round; failure reduces it to -1 HP. Damage from this spell cannot reduce HP below -1. If the target has less than half its maximum HP, a failed Will save skips the Fortitude save and reduces it to -1 HP. Exactly half HP still allows Fortitude. Temporary HP does not affect these thresholds. Mind-affecting immunity and spell resistance apply. As in CotW, constructs and vermin cannot be targeted. This spell can be undercast.

enGB:
Crush a creature's mind. A successful Will save deals 11d6 direct damage plus your caster level and sickens the target for 1 round. A failed Will save requires a Fortitude save: success deals 11d6 direct damage plus your caster level and sickens the target for 1 round; failure reduces it to -1 HP. Damage from this spell cannot reduce HP below -1. If the target has less than half its maximum HP, a failed Will save skips the Fortitude save and reduces it to -1 HP. Exactly half HP still allows Fortitude. Below half HP, the Will save also takes a -2 penalty. Temporary HP does not affect these thresholds. Mind-affecting immunity and spell resistance apply. As in CotW, constructs and vermin cannot be targeted. This spell can be undercast.

enGB: Use the persistent allocation toggles to distribute a total +4 morale bonus among Strength, Dexterity and Constitution in increments of 2. The total increases to +6 at bloodrager level 11 and +8 at 20. Then activate Controlled Bloodrage. It grants none of the ordinary bloodrage attack, damage, temporary hit point, Will or AC adjustments. It counts as bloodrage for bloodline powers and prerequisites. Native rage rounds, fatigue restrictions and Limitless Rage are retained. Charisma-, Dexterity- and Intelligence-based skills remain usable.

enGB: While paladins often collaborate with less righteous adventurers in order to further their causes, those who spend too much time around companions with particularly loose morals run the risk of adopting those same unscrupulous ideologies and methods. Such a vindictive bastard, as these fallen paladins are known, strikes out for retribution and revenge, far more interested in tearing down those who have harmed her or her companions than furthering a distant deity's cause.

enGB: Vindictive Bastards are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, with all types of armor (heavy, medium, and light), and with shields (except tower shields).

enGB: This creature has harmed you or one of your allies.
zhCN: This creature has harmed you or one of your allies.

enGB: A vindictive bastard is particularly ruthless against those who have harmed her or her allies. Once per day as a swift action, she can smite one target within sight who has dealt hit point damage to her or an ally. She adds her Charisma modifier to her attack rolls and adds her paladin level to damage rolls against the target of her smite. In addition, while vindictive smite is in effect, the vindictive bastard gains a deflection bonus equal to her Charisma bonus (if any) to her AC against attacks by the target of the smite. The vindictive smite effect remains until the target of the smite is dead or the next time the vindictive bastard rests and regains her uses of this ability. At 4th level and every 3 levels thereafter, the vindictive bastard can invoke her vindictive smite one additional time per day, to a maximum of seven times per day at 19th level.
